glasses_dana: Previous notes suggested bathroom_shelf_ba1 for early morning, but today at 12:26 it was at coffee_table_l1. This contradicts the "bathroom hub" pattern for mid-day. The location is highly volatile and time-dependent. Check bathroom_shelf_ba1 for pre-9 AM, coffee_table_l1 for mid-day (10:00-15:00), and nightstand_b1 for late night (post-22:00). Do not default to bathroom for all daytime queries.

water_bottle_dana: Previous notes suggested coffee_table_l1 for afternoon, but today at 19:54 it was at kitchen_table_k1. This indicates the bottle moves to the kitchen in the evening. Check coffee_table_l1 for mid-day (10:00-15:00) and kitchen_table_k1 for evening (post-18:00). The "living room hub" pattern does not apply to evening hours.

mug_dana: Previous notes assumed desk_o1 during work hours, but today it was at coffee_table_l1 at 09:22 and 11:14. This contradicts the "stays at office desk" pattern. The mug appears to be in the living room during the day. Check coffee_table_l1 for daytime locations.

book_dana: Previous notes suggested coffee_table_l1 for daytime, but today at 20:43 it was at couch_l1. This indicates the book moves to the couch in the evening, not just the coffee table. Check coffee_table_l1 for mid-day (10:00-15:00) and couch_l1 for evening (post-18:00). The "coffee table hub" pattern fails for evening hours.

glass_dana: Previous notes suggested counter_k1 for afternoon, but today at 22:19 it was at nightstand_b1. This confirms the late-night location is the bedroom. Check nightstand_b1 for late night locations.

General Pattern: The "coffee_table_l1 as central hub" heuristic is too broad. It applies to mid-day (10:00-15:00) for mugs, books, and water bottles, but fails for early morning glasses (bathroom), evening water bottles (kitchen), and evening books (couch). Time-of-day specificity is critical.
